monitor.title: Runtime monitoring
monitor.subtitle: Host resources and ZigFS request performance
monitor.refreshError: Unable to refresh monitoring data. Please retry.
monitor.retention: {seconds} s sampling · 10 s history · 24 h retention
monitor.retryHelp: Check the ZigFS connection and retry.
monitor.levelHelp: Scale: 0–{{max}}. Marker: peak of samples from the last minute ({{peak}}). Updated with real samples; this is not a capacity percentage.
monitor.levelUnavailable: No current sample. The level meter is unavailable.
monitor.resourceHelp: CPU: host and process. Memory: ZigFS. Disk I/O: process. Network: host, excluding loopback.
monitor.requestHelp: Rates use sampled counter differences. Latency percentiles are histogram upper bounds; no requests or values above 30 s are shown as gaps.
monitor.operationHelp: Cumulative totals since startup. Listings are a subset of requests, not additional HTTP traffic.
monitor.footnote: Live metrics refresh every 5 s; diagnostic details refresh every 30 s while expanded. Unreported measurements are not treated as zero. History snapshots are saved every minute and restored after restart; the most recent unsaved minute may be lost. Heap measures requested Application allocations, excluding libc and the startup arena. Host available memory on macOS is free + inactive memory.
monitor.noSamplesHelp: Waiting for supported measurements or request activity.
monitor.growthHelp: Uses up to 15 minutes of contiguous samples from this process run; at least 5 minutes are required. Growth is evidence for investigation, not proof of a leak.
monitor.alertsHelp: Rules persist across restarts. Acknowledgements and the latest 128 firing/recovery transitions are kept in memory.
monitor.noEvents: No alert transitions in this run.
monitor.locksHelp: Cumulative measurements for the metadata and identity locks only. Waiting time includes scheduler delay.
monitor.hotspotsHelp: Hotspots are opt-in, cumulative allocation/growth traffic at up to 64 call sites, not live memory. Addresses require the matching binary and symbols. Turning collection off preserves counts until restart. Native CPU and thread captures are available through tools/monitoring/capture.py on the server.
monitor.noHotspots: No recorded call sites. Enable collection and run a workload, then reload.
monitor.rulesHelp: Trigger above the threshold, or below it for available storage. Growth rules need continuous rising evidence. Duration is 0–3600 seconds; percentages are 0–100. Saving restarts evaluation timers.
monitor.invalidRules: Enter valid nonnegative thresholds and integer durations from 0 to 3600; percentages cannot exceed 100.
monitor.diagnosticsError: Unable to update or load diagnostics. Check your permissions and connection.
monitor.noRequestSamplesHelp: Latency and error rates need completed S3 requests. Admin page polling does not count. After object reads/writes, allow about 10 seconds for a history sample. Idle intervals remain empty.
monitor.requestSamplesUnavailable: S3 activity exists in the returned samples, but this metric is unavailable. Missing intervals remain empty; latency quantiles above 30 seconds are not estimated.
monitor.infoHostCpu: Host CPU utilization across all logical CPUs, normalized to 0–100%. The curve shows the last minute, including processes other than ZigFS.
monitor.infoHostMemory: Used host memory as a share of total memory, not just ZigFS. On macOS, available memory is estimated from free and inactive memory.
monitor.infoFilesystem: Used and total capacity of the filesystem containing the ZigFS data directory. Includes other files on that filesystem, not just stored objects.
monitor.infoRss: Current resident physical memory (RSS) of ZigFS, including resident heap, stacks, and mappings. The curve shows the last minute; peak is the process peak. Virtual memory is not physical memory usage.
monitor.infoProcessCpu: ZigFS process CPU utilization. 100% represents one fully used logical CPU; parallel work may exceed 100%.
monitor.infoDescriptors: Open file descriptors and the process limit, including files and network sockets. Approaching the limit can prevent opening files or accepting connections.
monitor.infoHeap: Outstanding memory tracked by the Application allocator and its peak. Excludes libc and startup arenas; this is not RSS.
monitor.infoQps: Completed S3 requests per second. Excludes Management API calls and dashboard polling; measures object workload activity.
monitor.infoActiveRequests: S3 requests currently being processed. Connection count includes connections that may be idle.
monitor.infoAllocations: Cumulative allocation and free counts from the Application allocator. Their difference does not directly measure leaked bytes.
monitor.infoAllocationFailures: Tracked memory allocation failures since process startup, useful for detecting memory pressure or allocation errors.
monitor.infoUptime: Elapsed runtime of the current ZigFS instance; resets on restart.
monitor.infoLoad: Host load averages over 1, 5, and 15 minutes, not CPU percentages. Interpret alongside logical CPU count. Unsupported platforms show no value.
monitor.infoStorageAvailable: Available space on the filesystem containing ZigFS data, useful for assessing write capacity; not a bucket quota.
monitor.infoWorkers: I/O runtime worker count and busy workers, including background tasks, for observing scheduling load.
monitor.infoCpuChart: Host and ZigFS CPU history. Host usage is normalized across CPUs; process usage uses 100% per logical CPU. Missing samples and restarts break the line.
monitor.infoMemoryChart: ZigFS RSS and Application heap history, showing peaks, recovery, and sustained growth. Their scopes differ; missing samples are not zero.
monitor.infoDiskChart: ZigFS process disk read and write rates in bytes per second, not disk capacity or total host disk traffic.
monitor.infoNetworkChart: Host network receive and send rates in bytes per second. May include other processes; not S3-only traffic.
monitor.infoLatency: P50, P95, and P99 duration estimates for completed S3 requests, in milliseconds, derived from histograms. No requests does not mean zero latency.
monitor.infoErrorChart: Server and client error shares in S3 requests, distinguishing service failures from request issues. No rate is estimated without completed requests.
monitor.infoTransferChart: S3 object upload and download byte rates, excluding network traffic from other host applications.
monitor.infoThreads: Operating-system thread count for ZigFS, including workers and background threads; not active requests.
monitor.infoBuckets: Number of buckets reported by this ZigFS instance, not the number of active requests.
monitor.infoObjects: Object count reported by this ZigFS instance, indicating object population rather than total bytes.

gateway.title: HTTPS gateway
gateway.description: Serve Admin and S3 over HTTPS without a separate reverse proxy.
gateway.dnsHelp: Point both DNS names to this server using your LAN DNS or hosts file. The gateway does not configure DNS or install trust on client devices.
gateway.portHelp: For a native process, use the same listen and external port (443 for a URL without a port). With container port forwarding, use the container listen port and the published external port. Keep HTTP available for recovery.
gateway.keyHelp: Use a certificate covering both domains and its matching unencrypted key. The key is stored privately and cannot be downloaded.
gateway.prepared: HTTPS candidate prepared. Configure DNS and trust before applying.
gateway.trustHelp: Download the CA certificate and verify its fingerprint through a trusted channel. macOS: import into the System keychain and trust for SSL. Windows: import into Trusted Root Certification Authorities. Mobile devices and CLI tools may need separate CA configuration. Never disable TLS verification.
gateway.previewHelp: Candidate addresses, or the active addresses if no candidate exists:
gateway.proxyHelp: For IAM conditions based on HTTPS or client IP, configure the actual gateway source in ZigFS Trusted Proxies. This is not enabled automatically.
gateway.serverCheckPassed: Local HTTPS and upstream checks passed. Client DNS and certificate trust still require browser verification.
gateway.clientCheckPassed: Both HTTPS entries verified from this browser.
gateway.clientCheckFailed: HTTPS verification failed. Check DNS, certificate trust, port mapping and redirects, then retry.
gateway.applyConfirmation: Switch the S3 Public URL to this HTTPS gateway? Existing signed links are not rewritten. Path-style addressing will be used.
gateway.rolledBack: Candidate discarded and pending changes rolled back.
gateway.fallbackHelp: Choose an address that remains available without this gateway. Existing signed URLs are not changed.
gateway.disableConfirmation: Update the S3 endpoint and stop the HTTPS gateway? Use the HTTP Admin entry to continue if necessary.
gateway.localSetupHelp: Prepare HTTPS first with names beneath zigfs.home.arpa. Download and run the helper on this Mac to configure DNS and trust the CA. Administrator authorization is required. Then verify from your browser; resolver status alone does not confirm certificate trust.
gateway.installCommand: Install DNS configuration and CA trust:
gateway.uninstallCommand: Remove the resolver and this CA certificate (HTTPS access will stop working):
gateway.stepPrepare: Step 1: Save and prepare your changes. This starts a candidate HTTPS entry without changing the current S3 public address.
gateway.stepVerify: Step 2: Configure DNS and certificate trust, then run the server and browser checks. Enable becomes available after browser verification.
gateway.stepApply: Step 3: Enable this verified configuration. This also updates the S3 public address used for new signed links.
gateway.stepActive: This configuration is active. Save and prepare again after editing any fields.
gateway.expiresSoon: Certificate expires within 30 days or has expired
gateway.automaticRenewal: Automatic leaf renewal: checked on startup and hourly; renews with the same CA when fewer than 30 days remain. CA rotation requires explicit maintenance.
gateway.manualRenewal: Imported certificate: no automatic renewal. Import a replacement before expiry; stage trust changes on another listener port.
gateway.windowsSetupTitle: Local access on this Windows PC
gateway.windowsSetupHelp: Prepare HTTPS with names beneath zigfs.home.arpa, then run the downloaded PowerShell helper on the Windows PC hosting Admin. Approve UAC to add managed hosts entries and trust this CA. Existing conflicting entries are not overwritten. Windows uses hosts here, not the macOS local DNS service. Restart the browser and verify HTTPS afterward.
gateway.resolutionIPHelp: IPv4 address of the HTTPS gateway. Use 127.0.0.1 for this computer or its LAN address (for example 192.168.1.20). This changes local DNS answers and Windows helper hosts entries, not the ZigFS upstream. Save and prepare, then verify before enabling. Other devices still need DNS configuration and CA trust; the built-in DNS listens on this computer only.
